records.shortCitation: Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, vol. 6, p. 780
records.fullCitation: Henner Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik 1925–1945. 10 vols. Uelzen: self-published; from vol. 2 Leverkusen: Pfau, 1987–2018. Vol. 6, (Foxtrott u.ä.) L–Q (2003), p. 780, entry “Mit dir möchte ich ziehn bis zum Ende der Welt”, marked SF for slow fox: Germany, 1931, music Kaper, Dr. B., words Rotter, Fritz, with the remark “Details unbekannt”. One disc is listed: EDBEL, catalogue number F 681, Orchester Dittke, the plus sign after the band name marking a vocal refrain. Digitised in the Digitale Bibliothek Thüringen from the copy in the Lippmann + Rau-Musikarchiv.
records.title: Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik 1925–1945, vol. 6: (Foxtrott u.ä.) L–Q
records.creator: Henner Pfau
records.researchNote: The citation as first recorded named eight volumes dated 1987 and carried the DOI of vol. 1, which covers titles A–C; the set runs to ten volumes published between 1987 and 2018, and the entry stands in vol. 6 of 2003. The lexicon’s own guide explains its conventions: SF marks a slow fox, and a plus sign after an orchestra name means the side carries a vocal. Its label key covers only the principal labels and does not expand EDBEL, so the issuing label behind that abbreviation is not settled here. The title is absent from the German national bibliography, the discographic title lists and the indexes of printed song collections, and no transfer of the disc has been traced; a similar but distinct title, “Mit dir möcht’ ich geh’n bis an’s Ende der Welt”, was composed by J. Pfeil and recorded in 1938.

records.fullCitation: Uwe Harten. "Gmeindl, Walter." Oesterreichisches Musiklexikon online. Vienna: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften. doi:10.1553/0x0001cf41. The article gives 31 December 1890 at Hainburg an der Donau as the date of birth and 1 September 1958 at Hainburg as the date of death, and traces the appointments at the Munich Hofoper from 1915, the teaching post under Schreker in Berlin from 1922 and the professorship of composition from 1929. The lexicon spells the forename Walter, without the h carried by this record. Accessed 6 August 2026.

records.shortCitation: Harten, "Gmeindl, Walter", Oesterreichisches Musiklexikon online
records.title: Oesterreichisches Musiklexikon online — Gmeindl, Walter
records.researchNote: The article calls Gmeindl a pedagogue before anything else. Schreker engaged him in Berlin as a Dozent in 1922 and, in 1929, as professor of composition and head of the orchestra school of the Musikhochschule, where he later took the conducting class as well; Sergiu Celibidache and Ernst Pepping were among his pupils. It is the teaching post held during Kaper’s Berlin years, which the archive documents in the event of private study, 1926–1930.

records.researchNote: The entry puts teaching at the centre of Mayer-Mahr’s life: he taught at the Klindworth-Scharwenka Conservatory in Berlin from 1892 to 1937, sat from 1907 on the jury of the Ibach competition at the Stern Conservatory and until 1933 on the senate of the Academy of Arts as an expert in music pedagogy. records.title: Léo Lelièvre (1899-1966)
records.creator: Bibliothèque nationale de France; Library of Congress
records.repository: Bibliothèque nationale de France (BnF); Library of Congress
records.researchNote: Two lyricists of the same name were at work in Paris in the 1930s: the chansonnier Léo Lelièvre (1872-1956), born in Reims, and his son Léo Edmond Lelièvre (1899-1966), a member of SACEM from November 1919, who wrote for the Casino de Paris beside Henri Varna and whose covers name him “Léo Lelièvre fils”, among them “Gosse de Paris” (1929) and “Le Tambour-major” from the revue “Paris qui brille” (1931). Both men worked on “Parade de France” in 1934: the Salabert prints of Maïotte Almaby’s créole numbers “La Vraie Créola” and “Ma Goulou Goulou” read “paroles françaises de Léo Lelièvre père”, while the Coda prints of the Jurmann–Kaper songs carry the undifferentiated form. The BnF catalogue is divided over those Coda prints: the notices for the illustrated issues and for the chant-et-piano prints of “C’est chez nous” and “Un baiser de femme sous un ciel de feu” link the son, whereas notices for three further printings of “Un baiser de femme sous un ciel de feu”, including Paul Saegel’s orchestral arrangement, still link the father. The son is preferred on three grounds: the printed “père” used for the other Lelièvre inside the same revue, the continuity of the Varna partnership at the Casino de Paris from 1929 onwards, and the weight of the revised catalogue notices.

records.title: Retour des Baléares
records.creator: Unsigned photograph
records.researchNote: The caption names the three men on deck and calls de Poligny the director, without naming a film. The photograph therefore shows the unit returning from the Balearic locations of that film, four months after the French release of the picture he had made with music by Kaper and Jurmann. No photographer or agency is credited beside it. This title is not among the issues digitised in Gallica, so the page is cited from the library’s subscription press service.

records.title: Kleine Bilder vom Semmering-Rennen
records.creator: Hans Schaukal (draughtsman)
records.researchNote: The page settles the identification. Its text calls him outright “der Theaterdirektor Franz Wenzler als Rennfahrer. Oder der Rennfahrer Franz Wenzler als Theaterdirektor. California Digital Newspaper Collection, University of California, Riverside. Accessed 26 August 2026.
records.title: It pays to be wacky, so — “The fly outflew the flea”
records.creator: Photographer unidentified
records.repository: California Digital Newspaper Collection, University of California, Riverside
records.researchNote: The caption places Shay in the middle of the three men and states his part in the song: he helped Terry Shand write the music to a lyric by Jimmie Eaton. The interview quotes him on how the piece came about — “Jimmie wrote the lyric and Terry and I fitted in the music. It has catchy tempo and words and that is all you need” — and an unnamed publisher sets out what launching a song then cost: three or four thousand dollars for printing, artwork and orchestration, and sixty to two hundred and fifty dollars a week for the men who placed it with radio singers. The dispatch is datelined Chicago and was carried by a wire service, so the same text and picture appeared in other papers.

records.title: Dokumenty Biura Odbudowy Stolicy jako podstawowe źródło wiedzy na temat architektury, konstrukcji i wyposażenia niezachowanych kamienic warszawskich projektu Henryka Stifelmana i Stanisława Weissa oraz Wacława Heppena i Józefa Napoleona Czerwińskiego
records.creator: Piotr Kilanowski
records.researchNote: Kilanowski identifies Wilcza 29 as a tenement designed by Henryk Stifelman and Stanisław Weiss. Drawing on the Capital City Reconstruction Office file APW 5069, he documents its post-war condition, the progressive collapse of the central part of the front building on 22 July 1945, the subsequent demolition of dangerous upper sections, and the surviving western and rear fragments. The article reproduces a 1945 floor-plan diagram and a photograph from the BOS file and distinguishes Wilcza 29 from the neighbouring Wilcza 29A, attributed to Wacław Heppen and Józef Napoleon Czerwiński.
